name: semantic-crosscheck
description: Cross-layer verification for an ontology plus semantic layer on PostgreSQL 17, for Codex and Claude Code.

interface.shortDescription: Prove that a PostgreSQL closure, SHACL rules, OWL reasoning and a Cube model agree.
interface.longDescription: Release v0.17.0: cross-check PostgreSQL 17 closures, SQL/SHACL rules, OWL/HermiT and Cube against independently authored gold SQL. Every requested V3 dimension/measure must exist in returned rows; explicit NULL remains valid, while missing members are invalid responses and never V4 mutation kills. The trusted-SQL lexical gate also recognizes quoted and schema-qualified known volatile calls while retaining supported aliases and literals. Undated filter/normalization mutation witnesses compare original and mutated generated key/value bags with bidirectional EXCEPT ALL, covering NULL-to-zero, missing keys, cancellation and MIN/MAX observability. Dated witnesses, dependency pins and report authority are unchanged. Current-data observability is not general SQL equivalence or a SQL sandbox. Rerun operational stages after upgrading.
defaultPrompt: Use semantic-crosscheck to run the synthetic demo end to end.
Use semantic-crosscheck to verify my crosscheck.toml against PostgreSQL and explain what is not proven.
